turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là một số bài báo khoa học mới nhất về **UAV** (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) vừa được đăng tải trên arXiv:

---

### 1. [Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11956v1)
- **Tác giả:** Akanksha Sneh, Krishna Ayyagari, Vivaswan Nawani, Shobha Sundar Ram
- **Lĩnh vực:** Xử lý tín hiệu (*eess.SP*)
- **Tóm tắt:** Đề xuất mô hình SAR đa tĩnh (bistatic) dựa trên UAV kết hợp cảm biến và truyền thông (ISAC) sử dụng dạng sóng IEEE 802.11ad. Phương pháp này tận dụng các gói tin truyền thông giữa UAV phát ISAC chính và UAV thu thụ động để đồng bộ thời gian/tần số, bù chuyển động và định vị 3D mục tiêu phức tạp trên địa hình dốc mà không cần hạ tầng phụ trợ.
- **Liên kết PDF:** [2611.11956v1.pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.11956v1)

---

### 2. [Correctness Metric Matters: NWD-Based Calibration Loss for Tiny Person Detection in UAV Infrared Imagery](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11735v1)
- **Tác giả:** Tian Zhang, Zhirong Su
- **Lĩnh vực:** Thị giác máy tính (*cs.CV*)
- **Tóm tắt:** Nghiên cứu bài toán phát hiện người kích thước siêu nhỏ (chiếm dưới 0.1% ảnh) trong ảnh hồng ngoại chụp từ UAV. Nhóm tác giả đề xuất thay thế hàm mất mát dựa trên IoU thông thường bằng hàm chuẩn hóa khoảng cách Wasserstein (NWD), giúp cải thiện độ tin cậy và hiệu chuẩn phát hiện (LaECE) trên bộ dữ liệu HIT-UAV mà không làm giảm mAP.
- **Liên kết PDF:** [2611.11735v1.pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.11735v1)

---

### 3. [Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11555v1)
- **Tác giả:** Sandesh Thapa, He Bai
- **Lĩnh vực:** Hệ thống điều khiển & Robot (*eess.SY, cs.RO*)
- **Tóm tắt:** Đề xuất bộ điều khiển hình học dựa trên học đồng thời tích phân (ICL) nhằm ước lượng trực tuyến khối lượng, độ lệch trọng tâm (CoM offset) và toàn bộ ma trận quán tính của UAV quadrotor khi mang tải hoặc bị rung lắc/dịch chuyển cảm biến, giúp bám quỹ đạo chính xác mà không cần dùng gia tốc kế hay đạo hàm số.
- **Liên kết PDF:** [2611.11555v1.pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.11555v1)

---

### 4. [FLAVOR: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11489v1)
- **Tác giả:** Yizhe Zhang, Jianping Li, Yilun Gao, Liangliang Yin, Pengfei Wan, Bisheng Yang
- **Lĩnh vực:** Robot (*cs.RO*)
- **Tóm tắt:** Giới thiệu kiến trúc bản đồ không gian - thời gian phân cấp FLAVOR cho UAV tự hành thám hiểm môi trường quy mô lớn. FLAVOR giới hạn bản đồ số liệu dày đặc ở phạm vi cục bộ xung quanh robot và dùng đồ thị topo thưa cho bối cảnh toàn cục, giúp giảm từ 94% đến 99% dung lượng bộ nhớ bản đồ và rút ngắn 31–41% thời gian thám hiểm.
- **Liên kết PDF:** [2611.11489v1.pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.11489v1)

---

### 5. [Missed Interferers in Ray-Traced Radio Maps: A Digital-Twin and Stochastic Geometry Study of Aerial Coverage](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10867v1)
- **Tác giả:** Saad Masrur, Ismail Guvenc
- **Lĩnh vực:** Mạng viễn thông & Xử lý tín hiệu (*eess.SP, cs.PF*)
- **Tóm tắt:** Đánh giá độ phủ sóng di động mặt đất đối với UAV bay ở độ cao 40–300m qua mô hình Digital Twin (bản sao số) của thành phố Raleigh. Nhóm tác giả phát hiện ra lỗi đánh giá sai tỷ số SINR trong các thuật toán ray-tracing Monte Carlo và đề xuất mô hình hình học ngẫu nhiên kết hợp thuật toán xác định LOS để tối ưu hóa hành lang bay an toàn cho UAV kết nối mạng tế bào.
- **Liên kết PDF:** [2611.10867v1.pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.10867v1)

items.title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.

items.title: Correctness Metric Matters: NWD-Based Calibration Loss for Tiny Person Detection in UAV Infrared Imagery
items.summary: Detection calibration aligns predicted confidence with empirical correctness. Existing calibration losses inherit their correctness definition from box regression, specifically IoU against a hard threshold. We show that this target is geometrically ill-posed for tiny objects in UAV infrared imagery, where persons occupy less than 0.1\% of the image. The same pixel error is penalized more heavily as the target shrinks, so binary prediction calibration (BPC) actively suppresses confidences that should be high. On HIT-UAV, BPC with an IoU target degrades image-level localization-aware ECE (LaECE) from 0.0689 to 0.0761, 0.0649 to 0.0733, and 0.0653 to 0.0682 across Low, Mid, and High signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) groups. We replace the IoU target with a continuous, scale-invariant normalized Wasserstein distance (NWD). The NWD target reduces LaECE\(_{\mathrm{NWD}}\) relative to BPC+IoU on all three groups (\(p<10^{-7}\)) with mAP neutral (0.9356 vs.\ 0.9347), and an independent center-offset anchor confirms that the gain is a genuine geometric correction. The improvement holds across a broad plateau of calibration weights. The NWD formulation requires no inference-time mapping layer. If a validation-fitted isotonic map is applied on top of it, calibration is lowered further, and the two corrections act on different components of the same error. The metric-level remedy has a measurable boundary. Target-background thermal pairing in the training distribution and detection-level aggregation under per-image detection-count heterogeneity lie outside it. Both are quantified independently of the NWD target.

items.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
items.summary: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.

items.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
items.summary: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.

items.title: Missed Interferers in Ray-Traced Radio Maps: A Digital-Twin and Stochastic Geometry Study of Aerial Coverage
items.summary: Ray-traced digital twins are increasingly used to plan where cellular-connected uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) can fly. In this paper, we build a Sionna RT digital twin around Raleigh, NC, with 18,591 buildings and two overlapping sub-1 GHz operator networks, and study the downlink signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of UAVs at 40-300 m. We show that the Monte Carlo radio-map solver of Sionna RT misses distant line-of-sight (LOS) interferers on aerial planes. With $10^7$ rays per sector and 5 m cells, it therefore underestimates the coverage at low SINR thresholds and overestimates it at high thresholds, by up to 26 percentage points at $\pm$2 dB and 50-100 m. Using a LOS-aware deterministic engine validated with Sionna's path solver, we then develop a stochastic geometry model with strongest-sector association and own-site leakage that matches the engine without fitting. The analysis shows that the interference grows logarithmically with the modeled network radius, so a twin that omits distant LOS sites overestimates the coverage, and that altitude mainly reduces the coverage at high SINR thresholds. Finally, selecting the better of two operators raises the minimum SINR along the best corridor by 1.0-3.9 dB up to 100 m.

items.title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.

items.title: Correctness Metric Matters: NWD-Based Calibration Loss for Tiny Person Detection in UAV Infrared Imagery
items.summary: Detection calibration aligns predicted confidence with empirical correctness. Existing calibration losses inherit their correctness definition from box regression, specifically IoU against a hard threshold. We show that this target is geometrically ill-posed for tiny objects in UAV infrared imagery, where persons occupy less than 0.1\% of the image. The same pixel error is penalized more heavily as the target shrinks, so binary prediction calibration (BPC) actively suppresses confidences that should be high. On HIT-UAV, BPC with an IoU target degrades image-level localization-aware ECE (LaECE) from 0.0689 to 0.0761, 0.0649 to 0.0733, and 0.0653 to 0.0682 across Low, Mid, and High signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) groups. We replace the IoU target with a continuous, scale-invariant normalized Wasserstein distance (NWD). The NWD target reduces LaECE\(_{\mathrm{NWD}}\) relative to BPC+IoU on all three groups (\(p<10^{-7}\)) with mAP neutral (0.9356 vs.\ 0.9347), and an independent center-offset anchor confirms that the gain is a genuine geometric correction. The improvement holds across a broad plateau of calibration weights. The NWD formulation requires no inference-time mapping layer. If a validation-fitted isotonic map is applied on top of it, calibration is lowered further, and the two corrections act on different components of the same error. The metric-level remedy has a measurable boundary. Target-background thermal pairing in the training distribution and detection-level aggregation under per-image detection-count heterogeneity lie outside it. Both are quantified independently of the NWD target.

items.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
items.summary: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.

items.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
items.summary: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.

items.title: Missed Interferers in Ray-Traced Radio Maps: A Digital-Twin and Stochastic Geometry Study of Aerial Coverage
items.summary: Ray-traced digital twins are increasingly used to plan where cellular-connected uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) can fly. In this paper, we build a Sionna RT digital twin around Raleigh, NC, with 18,591 buildings and two overlapping sub-1 GHz operator networks, and study the downlink signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of UAVs at 40-300 m. We show that the Monte Carlo radio-map solver of Sionna RT misses distant line-of-sight (LOS) interferers on aerial planes. With $10^7$ rays per sector and 5 m cells, it therefore underestimates the coverage at low SINR thresholds and overestimates it at high thresholds, by up to 26 percentage points at $\pm$2 dB and 50-100 m. Using a LOS-aware deterministic engine validated with Sionna's path solver, we then develop a stochastic geometry model with strongest-sector association and own-site leakage that matches the engine without fitting. The analysis shows that the interference grows logarithmically with the modeled network radius, so a twin that omits distant LOS sites overestimates the coverage, and that altitude mainly reduces the coverage at high SINR thresholds. Finally, selecting the better of two operators raises the minimum SINR along the best corridor by 1.0-3.9 dB up to 100 m.

Abstract—Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC)
frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar
sensing and wireless communication using common spectral
and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled Unmanned
Aerial Vehicles (UA V) for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)
focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target
imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UA V tomographic
SAR framework in which the IEEE 802.11ad waveform,
RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for
communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D)
localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate
how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC
transceiver UA V to a passive receiver UA V are exploited for
timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation,
and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary
infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We
evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive
targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations
modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The
results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared
with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay
between radar and communication performances are further
evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.
Index Terms—synthetic aperture radar, bistatic radar, UA V ,
ISAC, motion compensation
I. INTRODUCTION
UA Vs equipped with SAR are increasingly used for remote
sensing, surveillance, and situational awareness [1]–[4]. These
systems combine platform agility, fast deployment, and low
cost with SAR benefits of all-weather, day-night imaging,
and wide-area coverage. UA V-SAR is particularly useful when
traditional space-borne SAR is limited by long satellite revisit
times and when manned aircraft are difficult, unsafe, or
expensive to operate. Furthermore, recent advances in compact
millimeter wave (mmWave) transceivers, lightweight antennas,
onboard processing, and autonomous operation enable the
integration of high-performance mmWave SAR payloads on
small-to-medium UA Vs. The large available bandwidth at
mmWave frequencies provides fine range resolution, enabling
high-resolution imaging [5].
Monostatic UA V SAR systems, in which the transmitter
and receiver are on the same platform, are the most

to facilitating two-dimensional imaging along range and
cross-range. Interferometric [7], [8], bistatic [9], [10],
and multistatic [11], [12] configurations exploit additional
spatial, Doppler, and scattering diversity to enhance radar

second aperture across tracks for optimally reconstructing

- **Tận dụng gói tin truyền thông để đồng bộ:**

  - UAV phụ (Passive Receiver) nhận trực tiếp các gói tin truyền thông này (đường truyền tầm nhìn thẳng - LoS) để **tự đồng bộ thời gian và tần số**, đồng thời dùng nó làm tín hiệu tham chiếu để **bù chuyển động (motion compensation)** và xử lý tín hiệu phản xạ từ mục tiêu về máy thu.
  - **Không cần phần cứng phụ trợ:** UAV phụ không cần gắn thêm các thiết bị đồng bộ hoặc trạm mặt đất phức tạp.

---

### 3. Kết quả đánh giá
- **Kịch bản thử nghiệm:** Mô phỏng Monte Carlo để định vị 3D các mục tiêu phức tạp (như xe ô tô) di chuyển/nằm trên địa hình dốc gồ ghề, có tính đến các sai số dịch chuyển của UAV và sai số đồng bộ thực tế.
- **Hiệu quả:**
  - Đạt độ chính xác định vị 3D cao hơn rõ rệt so với các phương pháp định vị InSAR truyền thống.
  - Phân tích và đánh giá sự đánh đổi (trade-off) giữa hiệu năng truyền thông dữ liệu và độ nét/chính xác radar dưới các sơ đồ điều chế khác nhau.

Bistatic UA V-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using
Integrated Sensing and Communications
Transceivers
Akanksha Sneh,Member IEEE, Krishna Ayyagari ∗, Vivaswan Nawani∗, Shobha Sundar Ram,Senior
Member IEEE.
Abstract—Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC)
frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar
sensing and wireless communication using common spectral
and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled Unmanned
Aerial Vehicles (UA V) for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)
focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target
imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UA V tomographic
SAR framework in which the IEEE 802.11ad waveform,
RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for
communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D)
localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate
how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC
transceiver UA V to a passive receiver UA V are exploited for
timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation,
and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary
infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We
evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive
targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations
modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The
results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared
with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay
between radar and communication performances are further
evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.
Index Terms—synthetic aperture radar, bistatic radar, UA V ,
ISAC, motion compensation
I. INTRODUCTION
UA Vs equipped with SAR are increasingly used for remote
sensing, surveillance, and situational awareness [1]–[4]. These
systems combine platform agility, fast deployment, and low
cost with SAR benefits of all-weather, day-night imaging,
and wide-area coverage. UA V-SAR is particularly useful when
traditional space-borne SAR is limited by long satellite revisit
times and when manned aircraft are difficult, unsafe, or
expensive to operate. Furthermore, recent advances in compact
millimeter wave (mmWave) transceivers, lightweight antennas,
onboard processing, and autonomous operation enable the
integration of high-performance mmWave SAR payloads on
small-to-medium UA Vs. The large available bandwidth at
mmWave frequencies provides fine range resolution, enabling
high-resolution imaging [5].
Monostatic UA V SAR systems, in which the transmitter
and receiver are on the same platform, are the most

The first three authors are with the Indraprastha Institute of Information
Technology, Delhi, New Delhi 110020 India. E-mail:{akankshas,

popular SAR systems and are easiest to deploy in terms
of synchronization [1], [6]. However, they are limited
to facilitating two-dimensional imaging along range and
cross-range. Interferometric [7], [8], bistatic [9], [10],
and multistatic [11], [12] configurations exploit additional
spatial, Doppler, and scattering diversity to enhance radar
detection metrics and can be configured for three-dimensional
(3D) scene reconstruction. The theoretical foundations of
bistatic image formation through inversion was studied in
[10]. Other developments in 3D SAR imaging include
interferometric SAR (InSAR) to map heights of structures
[7], differential InSAR to monitor deformations [13] on
the Earth’s surface, and SAR tomography (TomoSAR) to
resolve multiple scatterers along the elevation axis, which
is also the focus of our work. Early demonstrations of
TomoSAR used multiple airborne baselines to synthesize a
second aperture across tracks for optimally reconstructing
elevation profiles [14]. Later developments used multipass
spaceborne designs, capable of interferometry, focusing on
long-term repeat-pass data to allow 3D focusing [15].
The authors in [16] introduced differential TomoSAR
schemes based on multidimensional spectral estimation
and multifaceted signal classification algorithms to address
temporal decorrelation. More recent methods used holographic
SAR tomography with circular airborne trajectories and
iterative adaptive reconstruction to provide super-resolution
elevation reconstruction [17]. While these advances have
significantly improved the 3D imaging capability of SAR
systems, their practical realization on distributed UA V
platforms introduces several implementation challenges.
Among these, maintaining synchronization between spatially
separated platforms is one of the most challenging
requirements for coherent SAR image formation.
Existing synchronization approaches for bistatic UA V SAR
focus on hardware solutions, involving specialized microwave
links, reference beacons, pilot exchanges, or precise timing
sources based on global navigation satellite systems or atomic
oscillators on both UA Vs [11], [18], [19]. Alternatively, to
reduce the hardware load, signal-processing-based algorithms
that estimate and compensate for residual timing and
phase errors directly from the received echoes, have been
proposed. This approach is, however, effective only with
high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and stable geometries [20],
[21]. Recently, a third approach has been investigated,
in which UA Vs are augmented with communication links
arXiv:2611.11956v1  [eess.SP]  9 Nov 2026

2
to address synchronization and data-handling challenges
in a distributed architecture. In [8], UA V-to-ground and
UA V-to-UA V connections facilitate real-time data transfer
and sensing-aware formation control for bistatic InSAR [8].
Coherent multistatic UA V SAR architectures have also been
explored in [12], in which a direct line-of-sight sidelink was
used as a phase reference for hardware synchronization.
But these approaches do not scale to tomographic or
3D localization. Bistatic TomoSAR has more recently been
achieved by repurposing an uplink communication signal to
reconstruct tomographic elevation images [22]. The authors
of [23] used orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing
(OFDM) pilots over line-of-sight links to provide timing
and phase references for bistatic SAR processing at a
ground-based station. Specialized two-way synchronization
chains with pulsed carrier exchanges have also enabled
high-precision bistatic InSAR in-flight experiments [24].
These studies have focused on the coexistence of radar and
communication systems, where communication waveforms are
used for synchronization, while separate conventional radar
waveforms are used for SAR imaging. Instead of using
auxiliary communication platforms as discussed above, it
is advantageous to consider ISAC transceivers to manage
synchronization and interference between communications and
radar.
Recent studies have explored waveform co-design strategies
to enable joint wireless communication and high-resolution
SAR imaging, in monostatic configurations or with centralized
or ground-based infrastructure [18], [25]. As a result,
they do not address the challenges of distributed bistatic
synchronization and motion compensation in UA V-based
tomographic SAR scenarios. In addition, most prior work is
limited to two-dimensional imaging or simplified point-target
models and does not address three-dimensional localization
of complex, distributed targets within an ISAC framework.
Furthermore, many studies assume stationary or ground-based
receivers and simplified motion models, which limit their
applicability to realistic UA V deployments involving mobile
platforms, elevated terrain, and dynamic flight trajectories.
In practical bistatic SAR systems, platform and target
motion cause significant image displacement, defocusing,
and localization errors whose severity depends on the
bistatic geometry and target kinematics [26], [27]. Hence,
